segment.text: Historical context [ edit ] Most of the French vocabulary now appearing in English was borrowed in the centuries following the Norman Conquest of 1066, when England came under the rule of Norman-speaking peoples.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4187-4400", "next_segment_id": "lseg-1ab1e56f01b7", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-b07dd5f73c72", "segment_id": "lseg-5d94509578d5", "source_id": "lsource-e3c4d32db662", "start_time": null, "text": "Historical context [ edit ] Most of the French vocabulary now appearing in English was borrowed in the centuries following the Norman Conquest of 1066, when England came under the rule of Norman-speaking peoples."}}

segment.text: After William the Conqueror had invaded England, subsequent rulers invaded other parts of the British Isles , distributing lands and property to Norman , Breton , Flemish , and French soldiers.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4400-4594", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c7012fc3aa61", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5d94509578d5", "segment_id": "lseg-1ab1e56f01b7", "source_id": "lsource-e3c4d32db662", "start_time": null, "text": "After William the Conqueror had invaded England, subsequent rulers invaded other parts of the British Isles , distributing lands and property to Norman , Breton , Flemish , and French soldiers."}}

segment.text: As a result, Old French became the language of high culture and government.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4594-4670", "next_segment_id": "lseg-07db82265c47", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-1ab1e56f01b7", "segment_id": "lseg-c7012fc3aa61", "source_id": "lsource-e3c4d32db662", "start_time": null, "text": "As a result, Old French became the language of high culture and government."}}

segment.text: With time, it evolved into Anglo-Norman French , a language widely used by the nobility and for legal affairs (See Law French ).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4670-4799", "next_segment_id": "lseg-0f93b8bb8be2", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c7012fc3aa61", "segment_id": "lseg-07db82265c47", "source_id": "lsource-e3c4d32db662", "start_time": null, "text": "With time, it evolved into Anglo-Norman French , a language widely used by the nobility and for legal affairs (See Law French )."}}

segment.text: The use of French and Norman in the kingdom was "extremely important" from William the Conqueror's coronation in 1066 until 1260.

segment.text: Main patterns of influence [ edit ] Old French had a "gw" sound, which mainly occurred in borrowings from old Germanic languages such as Frankish and Burgundian .

segment.text: In Parisian and other Langue d'oïl dialects, the "w" was elided, leaving "g".

segment.text: Examples of these follow: undo (consisting of prefix un- and root do ) untouchable (consisting of prefix un- , root touch , and suffix -able ) non-childproof (consisting of prefix non- , root child , and suffix -proof ) non-childproofable (consisting of prefix non- , root child , root proof , and suffix -able ) English words may consist of multiple prefixes: anti-pseudo-classicism (containing both an anti- prefix and a pseudo- prefix).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:1588-2028", "next_segment_id": "lseg-754a5eaffba5", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-12822bb73cfa", "segment_id": "lseg-16be36ffbd8d", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Examples of these follow: undo (consisting of prefix un- and root do ) untouchable (consisting of prefix un- , root touch , and suffix -able ) non-childproof (consisting of prefix non- , root child , and suffix -proof ) non-childproofable (consisting of prefix non- , root child , root proof , and suffix -able ) English words may consist of multiple prefixes: anti-pseudo-classicism (containing both an anti- prefix and a pseudo- prefix)."}}

segment.text: In English, all prefixes are derivational .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2028-2072", "next_segment_id": "lseg-34bb14010633", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-16be36ffbd8d", "segment_id": "lseg-754a5eaffba5", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "In English, all prefixes are derivational ."}}

segment.text: This contrasts with English suffixes, which may be either derivational or inflectional .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2072-2161", "next_segment_id": "lseg-805bbb82ec40", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-754a5eaffba5", "segment_id": "lseg-34bb14010633", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "This contrasts with English suffixes, which may be either derivational or inflectional ."}}

segment.text: Selectional restrictions [ edit ] As is often the case with derivational morphology, many English prefixes can only be added to bases of particular lexical categories (or "parts of speech").

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2161-2352", "next_segment_id": "lseg-3a1850908b47", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-34bb14010633", "segment_id": "lseg-805bbb82ec40", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Selectional restrictions [ edit ] As is often the case with derivational morphology, many English prefixes can only be added to bases of particular lexical categories (or \"parts of speech\")."}}

segment.text: For example, the prefix re- meaning "again, back" is only added to verb bases as in rebuild , reclaim , reuse , resell , re-evaluate , resettle .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2352-2498", "next_segment_id": "lseg-91b56ba93c9d", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-805bbb82ec40", "segment_id": "lseg-3a1850908b47", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "For example, the prefix re- meaning \"again, back\" is only added to verb bases as in rebuild , reclaim , reuse , resell , re-evaluate , resettle ."}}

segment.text: It cannot be added to bases of other lexical categories.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2498-2555", "next_segment_id": "lseg-673db607dd74", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-3a1850908b47", "segment_id": "lseg-91b56ba93c9d", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "It cannot be added to bases of other lexical categories."}}

segment.text: Thus, examples of re- plus a noun base (such as the ungrammatical *rehusband , *remonopoly ) or re- plus an adjective base ( *renatural , *rewise ) are virtually unattested.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2555-2729", "next_segment_id": "lseg-481c421a5f39", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-91b56ba93c9d", "segment_id": "lseg-673db607dd74", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Thus, examples of re- plus a noun base (such as the ungrammatical *rehusband , *remonopoly ) or re- plus an adjective base ( *renatural , *rewise ) are virtually unattested."}}

segment.text: [ 1 ] These selectional restrictions on what base a prefix can be attached to can be used to distinguish between otherwise identical-sounding prefixes.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2729-2881", "next_segment_id": "lseg-68606dc4cb2b", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-673db607dd74", "segment_id": "lseg-481c421a5f39", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 1 ] These selectional restrictions on what base a prefix can be attached to can be used to distinguish between otherwise identical-sounding prefixes."}}

segment.text: For instance, there are two different un- prefixes in English: one meaning "not, opposite of", the other meaning "reverse action, deprive of, release from".

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2881-3038", "next_segment_id": "lseg-8886094de9b4", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-481c421a5f39", "segment_id": "lseg-68606dc4cb2b", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "For instance, there are two different un- prefixes in English: one meaning \"not, opposite of\", the other meaning \"reverse action, deprive of, release from\"."}}

segment.text: The first prefix un- "not" is attached to adjective and participle bases while the second prefix un- "reverse action" is attached to either verb or noun bases.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3038-3198", "next_segment_id": "lseg-0e74cafaaf4c", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-68606dc4cb2b", "segment_id": "lseg-8886094de9b4", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "The first prefix un- \"not\" is attached to adjective and participle bases while the second prefix un- \"reverse action\" is attached to either verb or noun bases."}}

segment.text: Thus, English can have two words that are pronounced and spelled the same and have the same lexical category but have different meanings, different prefixes, a different internal morphological structure, and different internal bases that the prefixes are attached to: unlockable "not able to be locked" unlockable "able to be unlocked" In the first unlockable "not able to be locked", the prefix un- "not" is attached to an adjective base lockable (which, in turn, is composed of lock + -able ).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3198-3694", "next_segment_id": "lseg-9af230f2afaf", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-8886094de9b4", "segment_id": "lseg-0e74cafaaf4c", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Thus, English can have two words that are pronounced and spelled the same and have the same lexical category but have different meanings, different prefixes, a different internal morphological structure, and different internal bases that the prefixes are attached to: unlockable \"not able to be locked\" unlockable \"able to be unlocked\" In the first unlockable \"not able to be locked\", the prefix un- \"not\" is attached to an adjective base lockable (which, in turn, is composed of lock + -able )."}}

segment.text: This word has the following internal structure: [ un [ [ lock ] verb able ] adj ] adj In the second unlockable "able to be unlocked", the prefix un- "reverse action" is attached to a verb base lock , resulting in the derived verb unlock .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3694-3933", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5bea00966d7e", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-0e74cafaaf4c", "segment_id": "lseg-9af230f2afaf", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "This word has the following internal structure: [ un [ [ lock ] verb able ] adj ] adj In the second unlockable \"able to be unlocked\", the prefix un- \"reverse action\" is attached to a verb base lock , resulting in the derived verb unlock ."}}

segment.text: Subsequently, the -able suffix is added after the newly created unlock verb base deriving the adjective unlockable .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3933-4050", "next_segment_id": "lseg-7f5e99078758", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-9af230f2afaf", "segment_id": "lseg-5bea00966d7e", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Subsequently, the -able suffix is added after the newly created unlock verb base deriving the adjective unlockable ."}}

segment.text: This word has the following internal structure: [ [ un [ lock ] verb ] verb able ] adj Only certain verbs or nouns can be used to form a new verb having the opposite meaning.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4050-4225", "next_segment_id": "lseg-90b560930a98", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5bea00966d7e", "segment_id": "lseg-7f5e99078758", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "This word has the following internal structure: [ [ un [ lock ] verb ] verb able ] adj Only certain verbs or nouns can be used to form a new verb having the opposite meaning."}}

segment.text: In particular, using verbs describing an irreversible action produces words often considered nonsense, e.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4225-4331", "next_segment_id": "lseg-fd4f20d8828d", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-7f5e99078758", "segment_id": "lseg-90b560930a98", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "In particular, using verbs describing an irreversible action produces words often considered nonsense, e."}}

language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4331-4333", "next_segment_id": "lseg-571236a7e539", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-90b560930a98", "segment_id": "lseg-fd4f20d8828d", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "g."}}

language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4333-4367", "next_segment_id": "lseg-604870009413", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-fd4f20d8828d", "segment_id": "lseg-571236a7e539", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "unkill, unspend, unlose, unring ."}}

segment.text: These words may nevertheless be in occasional use for humorous or other effect.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4367-4447", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c495659ac451", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-571236a7e539", "segment_id": "lseg-604870009413", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "These words may nevertheless be in occasional use for humorous or other effect."}}

segment.text: Changes in lexical category [ edit ] Unlike derivational suffixes, English derivational prefixes typically do not change the lexical category of the base (and are so called class-maintaining prefixes).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4447-4649", "next_segment_id": "lseg-0853ecc8b28b", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-604870009413", "segment_id": "lseg-c495659ac451", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Changes in lexical category [ edit ] Unlike derivational suffixes, English derivational prefixes typically do not change the lexical category of the base (and are so called class-maintaining prefixes)."}}

segment.text: Thus, the word do , consisting of a single morpheme, is a verb, as is the word redo , which consists of the prefix re- and the base root do .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4649-4791", "next_segment_id": "lseg-159df7529ce6", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c495659ac451", "segment_id": "lseg-0853ecc8b28b", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Thus, the word do , consisting of a single morpheme, is a verb, as is the word redo , which consists of the prefix re- and the base root do ."}}

segment.text: However, there are a few prefixes in English that are class-changing in that the word resulting after prefixation belongs to a lexical category that is different from the lexical category of the base.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4791-4992", "next_segment_id": "lseg-44a59567a63a", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-0853ecc8b28b", "segment_id": "lseg-159df7529ce6", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "However, there are a few prefixes in English that are class-changing in that the word resulting after prefixation belongs to a lexical category that is different from the lexical category of the base."}}

segment.text: Examples of this type include a- , be- , and en- .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4992-5043", "next_segment_id": "lseg-10f38419a46a", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-159df7529ce6", "segment_id": "lseg-44a59567a63a", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Examples of this type include a- , be- , and en- ."}}

segment.text: a- typically creates adjectives from noun and verb bases: blaze (noun/verb) > ablaze (adj).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5043-5135", "next_segment_id": "lseg-d5a86239464e", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-44a59567a63a", "segment_id": "lseg-10f38419a46a", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "a- typically creates adjectives from noun and verb bases: blaze (noun/verb) > ablaze (adj)."}}

segment.text: The relatively unproductive be- creates transitive verbs from noun bases: witch (noun) > bewitch (verb).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5135-5240", "next_segment_id": "lseg-577443465f08", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-10f38419a46a", "segment_id": "lseg-d5a86239464e", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "The relatively unproductive be- creates transitive verbs from noun bases: witch (noun) > bewitch (verb)."}}

segment.text: en- creates transitive verbs from noun bases: slave (noun) > enslave (verb).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5240-5317", "next_segment_id": "lseg-57ebbc59c4e9", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-d5a86239464e", "segment_id": "lseg-577443465f08", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "en- creates transitive verbs from noun bases: slave (noun) > enslave (verb)."}}

language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5317-5328", "next_segment_id": "lseg-580c274293d4", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-577443465f08", "segment_id": "lseg-57ebbc59c4e9", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Native vs."}}

segment.text: non-native (neo-classical) prefixing [ edit ] Several English words are analyzed as a combination of a dependent affix and an independent base, such as those found in words like boy-hood or un-just .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5328-5528", "next_segment_id": "lseg-b7ab517fc787", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-57ebbc59c4e9", "segment_id": "lseg-580c274293d4", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "non-native (neo-classical) prefixing [ edit ] Several English words are analyzed as a combination of a dependent affix and an independent base, such as those found in words like boy-hood or un-just ."}}

segment.text: Following Marchand (1969), these types of words are formed by native word-formation processes.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5528-5623", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c9f66b84fa5f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-580c274293d4", "segment_id": "lseg-b7ab517fc787", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Following Marchand (1969), these types of words are formed by native word-formation processes."}}

segment.text: Other words in English (and also in French and German) are formed via foreign word-formation processes, particularly processes seen in Greek and Latin word-formation.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5623-5790", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c8761444c63e", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-b7ab517fc787", "segment_id": "lseg-c9f66b84fa5f", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Other words in English (and also in French and German) are formed via foreign word-formation processes, particularly processes seen in Greek and Latin word-formation."}}

segment.text: These word types are often known as neo-classical (or neo-Latin ) words and are often found in academic learned vocabulary domains (such as in science fields), as well as in inkhorn terms coined in the 17th and 18th centuries.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5790-6017", "next_segment_id": "lseg-0f659b2b7d56", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c9f66b84fa5f", "segment_id": "lseg-c8761444c63e", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "These word types are often known as neo-classical (or neo-Latin ) words and are often found in academic learned vocabulary domains (such as in science fields), as well as in inkhorn terms coined in the 17th and 18th centuries."}}

segment.text: Words of this nature are borrowed from either Greek or Latin or have been newly coined based upon Greek and Latin word-formation processes.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6017-6157", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5a35172a1ff8", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c8761444c63e", "segment_id": "lseg-0f659b2b7d56", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "Words of this nature are borrowed from either Greek or Latin or have been newly coined based upon Greek and Latin word-formation processes."}}

segment.text: It is possible to detect varying degrees of foreignness.

segment.text: [ 2 ] In some analytic frameworks, such neo-classical prefixes are excluded from analyses of English derivation on the grounds that they are not analyzable according to a mostly synchronic (that is, relatively productive or easily recognizable and relating to present-day idioms) English (that is, "native") basis.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6214-6529", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f94e3051429c", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5a35172a1ff8", "segment_id": "lseg-354f4a7d81ab", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 2 ] In some analytic frameworks, such neo-classical prefixes are excluded from analyses of English derivation on the grounds that they are not analyzable according to a mostly synchronic (that is, relatively productive or easily recognizable and relating to present-day idioms) English (that is, \"native\") basis."}}

segment.text: [ 3 ] Conceptualized thus, anglicized neo-classical English words such as deceive are not analyzed by Marchand as being composed of a prefix de- and a bound base -ceive but are rather analyzed as being composed of a single morpheme (although the Latin sources of these English words are analyzed as such, as "native" Latin components in the Latin language).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6529-6887", "next_segment_id": "lseg-ecb82a9d0b63", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-354f4a7d81ab", "segment_id": "lseg-f94e3051429c", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 3 ] Conceptualized thus, anglicized neo-classical English words such as deceive are not analyzed by Marchand as being composed of a prefix de- and a bound base -ceive but are rather analyzed as being composed of a single morpheme (although the Latin sources of these English words are analyzed as such, as \"native\" Latin components in the Latin language)."}}

segment.text: [ 4 ] Similarly, pairs such as defend/defense and double (or duple)/duplicity are not considered morphologically related in Marchand's treatment of English word formation and are thus excluded too, though they are regarded as derivatives of the shared roots in Jespersen's and Koizul's, while in others, they may be seen as allomorphs or variants (like deep/depth , a pair formed of Germanic components).

segment.text: However, not all foreign words are unanalyzable according to such an English basis: some foreign elements have been nativized and have become a part of productive English word-formation processes.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7292-7489", "next_segment_id": "lseg-970a75fd0204", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-ecb82a9d0b63", "segment_id": "lseg-a62930848756", "source_id": "lsource-6ab86d1263e1", "start_time": null, "text": "However, not all foreign words are unanalyzable according to such an English basis: some foreign elements have been nativized and have become a part of productive English word-formation processes."}}

segment.text: An example of such a now native English prefix is co- as in co-worker , which is ultimately derived from the Latin prefix com- (with its allomorphs co- , col- , con- , and cor- ); and ex- as in ex-soldier , which derives from the Latin ex- .

segment.text: Affixes Prefix Suffix Circumfix Duplifix Infix Libfix Interfix Transfix Simulfix Suprafix Disfix See also: Null morpheme v t e In linguistics , a suffix is an affix which is placed after the stem of a word.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2114-2321", "next_segment_id": "lseg-0ac67045ae3d", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c3832d1e62a1", "segment_id": "lseg-8777a8dbb61b", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "Affixes Prefix Suffix Circumfix Duplifix Infix Libfix Interfix Transfix Simulfix Suprafix Disfix See also: Null morpheme v t e In linguistics , a suffix is an affix which is placed after the stem of a word."}}

segment.text: Common examples are case endings , which indicate the grammatical case of nouns and adjectives, and verb endings, which form the conjugation of verbs.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2321-2472", "next_segment_id": "lseg-00f6309cad86", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-8777a8dbb61b", "segment_id": "lseg-0ac67045ae3d", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "Common examples are case endings , which indicate the grammatical case of nouns and adjectives, and verb endings, which form the conjugation of verbs."}}

segment.text: Suffixes can carry grammatical information ( inflectional endings) or lexical information ( derivational /lexical suffixes) .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2472-2598", "next_segment_id": "lseg-686346e7dece", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-0ac67045ae3d", "segment_id": "lseg-00f6309cad86", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "Suffixes can carry grammatical information ( inflectional endings) or lexical information ( derivational /lexical suffixes) ."}}

segment.text: [ 1 ] Inflection changes the grammatical properties of a word within its syntactic category .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2598-2692", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c4b96b13c1f0", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-00f6309cad86", "segment_id": "lseg-686346e7dece", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 1 ] Inflection changes the grammatical properties of a word within its syntactic category ."}}

segment.text: Derivational suffixes fall into two categories: class-changing derivation and class-maintaining derivation.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2692-2800", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f8f5de5eda37", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-686346e7dece", "segment_id": "lseg-c4b96b13c1f0", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "Derivational suffixes fall into two categories: class-changing derivation and class-maintaining derivation."}}

segment.text: Particularly in the study of Semitic languages , suffixes are called affirmatives , as they can alter the form of the words.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2800-2925", "next_segment_id": "lseg-bdf3c67364d8", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c4b96b13c1f0", "segment_id": "lseg-f8f5de5eda37", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "Particularly in the study of Semitic languages , suffixes are called affirmatives , as they can alter the form of the words."}}

segment.text: In Indo-European studies , a distinction is made between suffixes and endings (see Proto-Indo-European root ).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2925-3036", "next_segment_id": "lseg-7f2810b95f1a", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f8f5de5eda37", "segment_id": "lseg-bdf3c67364d8", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "In Indo-European studies , a distinction is made between suffixes and endings (see Proto-Indo-European root )."}}

segment.text: [ 5 ] Inflectional suffixes in Modern English include: Verbs [ edit ] -s third person singular simple present indicative active -ed past tense and past participle -t past tense (weak irregular) -ing present participle and gerund -en past participle (irregular) Nouns [ edit ] -s plural number -en plural number (irregular) Adjectives and adverbs [ edit ] -er comparative degree -est superlative degree Derivation [ edit ] Derivational suffixes can be divided into two categories: class-changing derivation and class-maintaining derivation.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5317-5857", "next_segment_id": "lseg-a2679c895818", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5bf141881ff1", "segment_id": "lseg-2db041fa0104", "source_id": "lsource-882e043c705b", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 5 ] Inflectional suffixes in Modern English include: Verbs [ edit ] -s third person singular simple present indicative active -ed past tense and past participle -t past tense (weak irregular) -ing present participle and gerund -en past participle (irregular) Nouns [ edit ] -s plural number -en plural number (irregular) Adjectives and adverbs [ edit ] -er comparative degree -est superlative degree Derivation [ edit ] Derivational suffixes can be divided into two categories: class-changing derivation and class-maintaining derivation."}}

segment.text: [ 6 ] In English, they include -ly (usually changes adjectives into adverbs, but also some nouns into adjectives) -al / -ual (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -ic / -ical (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -ish (usually changes nouns into adjectives/class-maintaining, with the word class remaining an adjective) -ful (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -oid (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -like (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -less (usually changes nouns into adjectives) -able / -ible (usually changes verbs into adjectives) -ant (usually changes verbs into nouns, often referring to a human agent) -tion / -ion / -ation (usually changes verbs into nouns) -ment (usually changes verbs into nouns) -ity (usually changes adjectives into nouns) -ness (usually changes adjectives into nouns) -fy (usually changes nouns into verbs) -ise / -ize (usually changes nouns into verbs) -ess (usually class-maintaining, with the word class remaining a noun) -ism (usually class-maintaining, with the word class remaining a noun) -ist (usually class-maintaining, with the word class remaining a noun) -hood (usually class-maintaining, with the word class remaining a noun) -logy / -ology (usually class-maintaining, with the word class remaining a noun) -um (usually) museum; stadium; auditorium; aquarium; planetarium; medium -wise From wīse ("manner, way, condition, direction") Altered pronunciation in English [ edit ] A suffix will often change the stress or accent pattern of a multi-syllable word, altering the phoneme pattern of the root word even if the root's morphology does not change.

segment.text: [ 1 ] The English language , like many others, uses compounds frequently.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2682-2756", "next_segment_id": "lseg-269988fe546e", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-154193e1440a", "segment_id": "lseg-76d787a4b8a1", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 1 ] The English language , like many others, uses compounds frequently."}}

segment.text: English compounds may be classified in several ways, such as the word classes or the semantic relationship of their components.

segment.text: History [ edit ] English inherits the ability to form compounds from its parent the Proto-Indo-European language and expands on it.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:2884-3016", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5d6deb901e54", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-269988fe546e", "segment_id": "lseg-1ae4d9b43182", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "History [ edit ] English inherits the ability to form compounds from its parent the Proto-Indo-European language and expands on it."}}

segment.text: [ 2 ] Close to two-thirds of the words in the Old English poem Beowulf are found to be compounds.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3016-3114", "next_segment_id": "lseg-d4e799961d50", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-1ae4d9b43182", "segment_id": "lseg-5d6deb901e54", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 2 ] Close to two-thirds of the words in the Old English poem Beowulf are found to be compounds."}}

segment.text: [ 3 ] Of all the types of word-formation in English, compounding is said to be the most productive.

segment.text: Most English compound nouns that consist of more than two words can be constructed recursively by combining two words at a time.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3475-3604", "next_segment_id": "lseg-fbc7ab91e7b6", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-dad7f31c81c3", "segment_id": "lseg-8f3043ed9125", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Most English compound nouns that consist of more than two words can be constructed recursively by combining two words at a time."}}

segment.text: Combining "science" and "fiction", and then combining the resulting compound with "writer", for example, can construct the compound "science fiction writer" or "science-fiction writer".

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3604-3790", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f539d6660dbf", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-8f3043ed9125", "segment_id": "lseg-fbc7ab91e7b6", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Combining \"science\" and \"fiction\", and then combining the resulting compound with \"writer\", for example, can construct the compound \"science fiction writer\" or \"science-fiction writer\"."}}

segment.text: Some compounds, such as salt and pepper or mother-of-pearl , cannot be constructed in this way, however.

segment.text: Orthography: open, hyphenated, or solid (closed up) [ edit ] English uses many open compound nouns, a large subclass of which, by convention in accepted English orthography , are not closed up (not solidified) and are sometimes optionally hyphenated in attributive position (that is, when functioning as a noun adjunct ).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:3895-4217", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c78edb03f655", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f539d6660dbf", "segment_id": "lseg-65a891e0ea3b", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Orthography: open, hyphenated, or solid (closed up) [ edit ] English uses many open compound nouns, a large subclass of which, by convention in accepted English orthography , are not closed up (not solidified) and are sometimes optionally hyphenated in attributive position (that is, when functioning as a noun adjunct )."}}

segment.text: Examples are high school , kidney disease , and file format .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4217-4279", "next_segment_id": "lseg-d06820f95f7c", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-65a891e0ea3b", "segment_id": "lseg-c78edb03f655", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Examples are high school , kidney disease , and file format ."}}

segment.text: Although some other languages would close up these nouns' components (for example, German usually does so), English has a tendency whereby it closes up only certain ones, usually only ones in which the head noun is monosyllabic (and even within that category, only sometimes, and in a way that is not fully standardized ).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:4279-4602", "next_segment_id": "lseg-4a3e48567c56", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c78edb03f655", "segment_id": "lseg-d06820f95f7c", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Although some other languages would close up these nouns' components (for example, German usually does so), English has a tendency whereby it closes up only certain ones, usually only ones in which the head noun is monosyllabic (and even within that category, only sometimes, and in a way that is not fully standardized )."}}

segment.text: For example, data set and dataset , or file name and filename , are accepted alternative forms, but file format , data format , and data analysis , which have multisyllabic heads ( format and analysis ), can only be spelled as open in accepted English orthography.

segment.text: This pattern holds for countless nouns with few exceptions.

segment.text: For the class with monosyllabic heads, there is a tendency that "compounds tend to solidify as they age," [ 5 ] : 368 which is how a term such as data set becomes dataset , pin-up becomes pinup , [ 5 ] : 368 coal mine becomes coalmine , bottle cap becomes bottlecap , and so on.

segment.text: Such alternative forms usually continue to coexist in accepted use; style guides often convene on preferred dictionaries as a way of achieving consistency, by declaring that the headword form there will be the default styling for each such term.

segment.text: Types of compound nouns [ edit ] Native English compound [ edit ] Since English is a mostly analytic language , unlike most other Germanic languages , it creates compounds by concatenating words without case markers .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5452-5670", "next_segment_id": "lseg-834e27390b5f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-2e5b3a8ddbd6", "segment_id": "lseg-f2aa3eef8201", "source_id": "lsource-504cde9bd958", "start_time": null, "text": "Types of compound nouns [ edit ] Native English compound [ edit ] Since English is a mostly analytic language , unlike most other Germanic languages , it creates compounds by concatenating words without case markers ."}}

segment.text: However, there are a few dozen common verb-object compounds – mostly dating from the 16th century and mostly with negative connotations – which have the opposite French order and which do not have a suffix -er .

segment.text: For example, a black board, adjective plus noun, is any board that is black, and has equal stress on both elements.

segment.text: A compound modifier is a sequence of modifiers of a noun that function as a single unit.

segment.text: It consists of two or more words (adjectives, gerunds, or nouns) of which the left-hand component modifies the right-hand one, as in "the dark-green dress": dark modifies the green that modifies dress .

segment.text: Hyphenated compound modifiers [ edit ] Major style guides advise consulting a dictionary to determine whether a compound modifier should be hyphenated; the dictionary's hyphenation should be followed even when the compound modifier follows a noun (that is, regardless of whether in attributive or predicative position), because they are permanent compounds [ 11 ] [ 12 ] (whereas the general rule with temporary compounds is that hyphens are omitted in the predicative position because they are used only when necessary to prevent misreading, which is usually only in the attributive position, and even there, only on a case-by-case basis).

segment.text: [ 13 ] [ 14 ] Generally, a compound modifier is hyphenated if the hyphen helps the reader differentiate a compound modifier from two adjacent modifiers that modify the noun independently.

segment.text: Hyphenated compound modifiers may have been formed originally by an adjective preceding a noun, when this phrase in turn precedes another noun: "Round table" → " round-table discussion " "Blue sky" → " blue-sky law " "Red light" → " red-light district " "Four wheels" → " four-wheel drive " (historically, the singular or root is used, not the plural ) Others may have originated with a verb preceding an adjective or adverb: "Feel good" → "feel-good factor" "Buy now, pay later" → "buy-now pay-later purchase" Yet others are created with an original verb preceding a preposition .

segment.text: [ 14 ] It evolved from the idea of creating a type of English that can be learned more easily than regular British or American English and that serves as a tool for successful global communication.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:23944-24084", "next_segment_id": "lseg-7fe0c6c65b13", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-0e73d36e3425", "segment_id": "lseg-7ec0f11bbbdf", "source_id": "lsource-0158de403c15", "start_time": null, "text": "Dual standard [ edit ] Two approaches to International English are the individualistic and inclusive approach and the new dialect approach."}}

segment.text: The individualistic approach gives control to individual authors to write and spell as they wish (within purported standard conventions) and to accept the validity of differences.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:24084-24264", "next_segment_id": "lseg-213581a476e6", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-7ec0f11bbbdf", "segment_id": "lseg-7fe0c6c65b13", "source_id": "lsource-0158de403c15", "start_time": null, "text": "The individualistic approach gives control to individual authors to write and spell as they wish (within purported standard conventions) and to accept the validity of differences."}}

segment.text: The Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English , published in 1999, is a descriptive study of both American and British English in which each chapter follows individual spelling conventions according to the preference of the main editor of that chapter.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:24264-24521", "next_segment_id": "lseg-38ee91d11f25", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-7fe0c6c65b13", "segment_id": "lseg-213581a476e6", "source_id": "lsource-0158de403c15", "start_time": null, "text": "The Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English , published in 1999, is a descriptive study of both American and British English in which each chapter follows individual spelling conventions according to the preference of the main editor of that chapter."}}

segment.text: The new dialect approach appears in The Cambridge Guide to English Usage (Peters, 2004), which attempts to avoid any language bias and accordingly uses an idiosyncratic international spelling system of mixed American and British forms.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:24521-24757", "next_segment_id": "lseg-126e0467287d", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-213581a476e6", "segment_id": "lseg-38ee91d11f25", "source_id": "lsource-0158de403c15", "start_time": null, "text": "The new dialect approach appears in The Cambridge Guide to English Usage (Peters, 2004), which attempts to avoid any language bias and accordingly uses an idiosyncratic international spelling system of mixed American and British forms."}}

segment.text: Qualifications [ edit ] Standardised testing in International English for non-native English language speakers has existed for a while.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:24757-24893", "next_segment_id": "lseg-b9fc96b9228a", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-38ee91d11f25", "segment_id": "lseg-126e0467287d", "source_id": "lsource-0158de403c15", "start_time": null, "text": "Qualifications [ edit ] Standardised testing in International English for non-native English language speakers has existed for a while."}}

segment.text: Learners can use their local dialect of English so it does not matter if they use British or American spelling.

segment.text: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS) is recognised in countries such as the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand and is the world's most popular English language test for higher education and immigration.

segment.text: [ 13 ] History [ edit ] The English Language Testing Service (ELTS), as IELTS was then known, was launched in 1980 by Cambridge English Language Assessment (then known as "UCLES") and the British Council .

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:5896-6102", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5743ad3d17d5", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-70c39f72a621", "segment_id": "lseg-711f98dfe56a", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 13 ] History [ edit ] The English Language Testing Service (ELTS), as IELTS was then known, was launched in 1980 by Cambridge English Language Assessment (then known as \"UCLES\") and the British Council ."}}

segment.text: It had an innovative format, which reflected changes in language learning and teaching, including the growth in 'communicative' language learning and 'English for specific purposes'.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6102-6285", "next_segment_id": "lseg-ea6c2a2357c6", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-711f98dfe56a", "segment_id": "lseg-5743ad3d17d5", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "It had an innovative format, which reflected changes in language learning and teaching, including the growth in 'communicative' language learning and 'English for specific purposes'."}}

segment.text: Test tasks were intended to reflect the use of English language in the 'real world'.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6285-6370", "next_segment_id": "lseg-654c2d23e471", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5743ad3d17d5", "segment_id": "lseg-ea6c2a2357c6", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Test tasks were intended to reflect the use of English language in the 'real world'."}}

segment.text: During the 1980s, test taker numbers were low (4,000 in 1981 rising to 10,000 in 1985) and there were practical difficulties administering the test.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6370-6519", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f2bdf767dd88", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-ea6c2a2357c6", "segment_id": "lseg-654c2d23e471", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "During the 1980s, test taker numbers were low (4,000 in 1981 rising to 10,000 in 1985) and there were practical difficulties administering the test."}}

segment.text: As a result, the IELTS Revision Project was set up to oversee the redesign of the test.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6519-6607", "next_segment_id": "lseg-9d440befac33", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-654c2d23e471", "segment_id": "lseg-f2bdf767dd88", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "As a result, the IELTS Revision Project was set up to oversee the redesign of the test."}}

segment.text: In order to have international participation in the redesign, the International Development Program of Australian Universities and Colleges ( IDP ), now known as IDP: IELTS Australia , joined Cambridge English Language Assessment and the British Council to form the international IELTS partnership which delivers the test to this day.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6607-6942", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f7005486660f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f2bdf767dd88", "segment_id": "lseg-9d440befac33", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "In order to have international participation in the redesign, the International Development Program of Australian Universities and Colleges ( IDP ), now known as IDP: IELTS Australia , joined Cambridge English Language Assessment and the British Council to form the international IELTS partnership which delivers the test to this day."}}

segment.text: This international partnership was reflected in the new name for the test: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:6942-7076", "next_segment_id": "lseg-04e8a27ed3df", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-9d440befac33", "segment_id": "lseg-f7005486660f", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "This international partnership was reflected in the new name for the test: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS)."}}

language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7076-7101", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f64248e5796f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f7005486660f", "segment_id": "lseg-04e8a27ed3df", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "IELTS went live in 1989."}}

segment.text: Test takers took two non-specialised modules, Listening and Speaking, and two specialised modules, Reading and Writing.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7101-7221", "next_segment_id": "lseg-68684d199b66", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-04e8a27ed3df", "segment_id": "lseg-f64248e5796f", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Test takers took two non-specialised modules, Listening and Speaking, and two specialised modules, Reading and Writing."}}

segment.text: Test taker numbers rose by approximately 15% per year and by 1995 there were 43,000 test takers in 210 test centres around the world.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7221-7355", "next_segment_id": "lseg-d1924b405434", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f64248e5796f", "segment_id": "lseg-68684d199b66", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Test taker numbers rose by approximately 15% per year and by 1995 there were 43,000 test takers in 210 test centres around the world."}}

segment.text: IELTS was revised again in 1995, with three main changes: There was one Academic Reading Module and one Academic Writing Module (previously there had been a choice of three field-specific Reading and Writing modules) The thematic link between the Reading and Writing tasks was removed to avoid confusing the assessment of reading and writing ability The General Training Reading and Writing modules were brought into line with the Academic Reading and Writing modules (same timing, length of responses, reporting of scores).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7355-7880", "next_segment_id": "lseg-1d0f6edb26c2", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-68684d199b66", "segment_id": "lseg-d1924b405434", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "IELTS was revised again in 1995, with three main changes: There was one Academic Reading Module and one Academic Writing Module (previously there had been a choice of three field-specific Reading and Writing modules) The thematic link between the Reading and Writing tasks was removed to avoid confusing the assessment of reading and writing ability The General Training Reading and Writing modules were brought into line with the Academic Reading and Writing modules (same timing, length of responses, reporting of scores)."}}

segment.text: Further revisions went live in 2001 (revised Speaking Test) and 2005 (new assessment criteria for the Writing test).

segment.text: [ 14 ] IELTS characteristics [ edit ] IELTS Academic and IELTS General Training are designed to cover the full range of abilities from non-user or middle user to expert user.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:7997-8172", "next_segment_id": "lseg-01a676fceccd", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-1d0f6edb26c2", "segment_id": "lseg-6ac1c759b085", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 14 ] IELTS characteristics [ edit ] IELTS Academic and IELTS General Training are designed to cover the full range of abilities from non-user or middle user to expert user."}}

segment.text: The Academic version is for test takers who want to study at the tertiary level in an English-speaking country or seek professional registration.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8172-8318", "next_segment_id": "lseg-d7ca39c7f32d", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-6ac1c759b085", "segment_id": "lseg-01a676fceccd", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The Academic version is for test takers who want to study at the tertiary level in an English-speaking country or seek professional registration."}}

segment.text: The General Training version is for test takers who want to work, train, study at a secondary school or migrate to an English-speaking country.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8318-8462", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c4c540740ba6", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-01a676fceccd", "segment_id": "lseg-d7ca39c7f32d", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The General Training version is for test takers who want to work, train, study at a secondary school or migrate to an English-speaking country."}}

segment.text: [ 15 ] The difference between the Academic and General Training versions is the content, context, and purpose of the tasks.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8462-8586", "next_segment_id": "lseg-a31665af72bc", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-d7ca39c7f32d", "segment_id": "lseg-c4c540740ba6", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 15 ] The difference between the Academic and General Training versions is the content, context, and purpose of the tasks."}}

segment.text: All other features, such as timing allocation, length of written responses, and reporting of scores, are the same.

segment.text: [ 16 ] IELTS Academic and General Training both incorporate the following features: IELTS tests the ability to listen , read , write and speak in English.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8701-8856", "next_segment_id": "lseg-36561b0b15ab", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-a31665af72bc", "segment_id": "lseg-6a72fe3a7f4f", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 16 ] IELTS Academic and General Training both incorporate the following features: IELTS tests the ability to listen , read , write and speak in English."}}

segment.text: The speaking module is a key component of IELTS.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8856-8905", "next_segment_id": "lseg-fac5ff9cad65", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-6a72fe3a7f4f", "segment_id": "lseg-36561b0b15ab", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The speaking module is a key component of IELTS."}}

segment.text: It is conducted in the form of a one-to-one interview with an examiner which can occur face to face or even through a video conference.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:8905-9041", "next_segment_id": "lseg-a517a0c222ef", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-36561b0b15ab", "segment_id": "lseg-fac5ff9cad65", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "It is conducted in the form of a one-to-one interview with an examiner which can occur face to face or even through a video conference."}}

segment.text: The examiner assesses the test taker as they are speaking.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:9041-9100", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5ad8126600fd", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-fac5ff9cad65", "segment_id": "lseg-a517a0c222ef", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The examiner assesses the test taker as they are speaking."}}

segment.text: The speaking session is also recorded for monitoring and for re-marking in case of an appeal against the score given.

segment.text: A variety of accents and writing styles have been presented in test materials in order to minimize linguistic bias.

segment.text: IELTS test structure [ edit ] Modules [ edit ] There are two modules of the IELTS: Academic Module General Training Module There is also a separate test offered by the IELTS test partners, called IELTS Life Skills : IELTS Academic is intended for those who want to enroll in universities and other institutions of higher education and for professionals such as medical doctors, engineers and nurses who want to study or practice in an English-speaking country.

segment.text: Mainly for those who is trying for non-immigrant student visa.

segment.text: Total Test Time 2 hours and 45 minutes [ 19 ] Note 1: Listening, Reading and Writing are completed in one sitting.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11069-11184", "next_segment_id": "lseg-60477085b9e9", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-df458ae862fe", "segment_id": "lseg-79b8d573557d", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Total Test Time 2 hours and 45 minutes [ 19 ] Note 1: Listening, Reading and Writing are completed in one sitting."}}

segment.text: The Speaking test may be taken on the same day or up to seven days before or after the other tests.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11184-11284", "next_segment_id": "lseg-ff58a7a6ff5a", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-79b8d573557d", "segment_id": "lseg-60477085b9e9", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The Speaking test may be taken on the same day or up to seven days before or after the other tests."}}

segment.text: Note 2: All test takers take the same Listening and Speaking tests, while the Reading and Writing tests differ depending on whether the test taker is taking the Academic or General Training versions of the test.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11284-11496", "next_segment_id": "lseg-205da56c5b09", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-60477085b9e9", "segment_id": "lseg-ff58a7a6ff5a", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Note 2: All test takers take the same Listening and Speaking tests, while the Reading and Writing tests differ depending on whether the test taker is taking the Academic or General Training versions of the test."}}

segment.text: Note 3: The 10 minutes transfer time is for the paper-based option of the test.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11496-11576", "next_segment_id": "lseg-6216cd55a0ac", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-ff58a7a6ff5a", "segment_id": "lseg-205da56c5b09", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Note 3: The 10 minutes transfer time is for the paper-based option of the test."}}

segment.text: For the computer-delivered option, candidates will be given 2 minutes (at the end of the test) to re-check their answers.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11576-11698", "next_segment_id": "lseg-04a0fdd89762", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-205da56c5b09", "segment_id": "lseg-6216cd55a0ac", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "For the computer-delivered option, candidates will be given 2 minutes (at the end of the test) to re-check their answers."}}

segment.text: [ 20 ] Listening [ edit ] The module comprises four sections, with ten questions in each section.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11698-11796", "next_segment_id": "lseg-b35e772bc4c3", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-6216cd55a0ac", "segment_id": "lseg-04a0fdd89762", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 20 ] Listening [ edit ] The module comprises four sections, with ten questions in each section."}}

segment.text: It takes around 40 (paper-based) or 32 (computer-delivered) minutes: 30 for testing, plus 10 for transferring the answers to an answer sheet (paper-based) or 2 for re-checking the answers (computer-delivered).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:11796-12006", "next_segment_id": "lseg-f0796b0a9e2b", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-04a0fdd89762", "segment_id": "lseg-b35e772bc4c3", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "It takes around 40 (paper-based) or 32 (computer-delivered) minutes: 30 for testing, plus 10 for transferring the answers to an answer sheet (paper-based) or 2 for re-checking the answers (computer-delivered)."}}

segment.text: [ 21 ] [ 20 ] Sections 1 and 2 are about everyday, social situations.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12006-12076", "next_segment_id": "lseg-eb3a4704744f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-b35e772bc4c3", "segment_id": "lseg-f0796b0a9e2b", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 21 ] [ 20 ] Sections 1 and 2 are about everyday, social situations."}}

segment.text: Section 1 has a conversation between two speakers (for example, a conversation about travel arrangements) Section 2 has one person speaking (for example, a speech about local facilities).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12076-12264", "next_segment_id": "lseg-7806a7978b14", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-f0796b0a9e2b", "segment_id": "lseg-eb3a4704744f", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Section 1 has a conversation between two speakers (for example, a conversation about travel arrangements) Section 2 has one person speaking (for example, a speech about local facilities)."}}

segment.text: Sections 3 and 4 are about educational and training situations Section 3 is a conversation between two main speakers (for example, a discussion between two university students, perhaps guided by a tutor) Section 4 has one person speaking about an academic subject.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12264-12529", "next_segment_id": "lseg-5ff2071d089e", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-eb3a4704744f", "segment_id": "lseg-7806a7978b14", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Sections 3 and 4 are about educational and training situations Section 3 is a conversation between two main speakers (for example, a discussion between two university students, perhaps guided by a tutor) Section 4 has one person speaking about an academic subject."}}

segment.text: [ 22 ] Each section begins with a short introduction telling the test taker about the situation and the speakers.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12529-12643", "next_segment_id": "lseg-a2b6314b9db1", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-7806a7978b14", "segment_id": "lseg-5ff2071d089e", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 22 ] Each section begins with a short introduction telling the test taker about the situation and the speakers."}}

segment.text: Then they have some time to look through the questions.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12643-12699", "next_segment_id": "lseg-7195edb01be2", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-5ff2071d089e", "segment_id": "lseg-a2b6314b9db1", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Then they have some time to look through the questions."}}

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12699-12869", "next_segment_id": "lseg-bce0b5377542", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-a2b6314b9db1", "segment_id": "lseg-7195edb01be2", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The questions are in the same order as the information in the recording, so the answer to the first question will be before the answer to the second question, and so on."}}

segment.text: [ 22 ] The first three sections have a break in the middle allowing test takers to look at the remaining questions.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12869-12985", "next_segment_id": "lseg-1b4c3b2110d4", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-7195edb01be2", "segment_id": "lseg-bce0b5377542", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 22 ] The first three sections have a break in the middle allowing test takers to look at the remaining questions."}}

segment.text: Each section is heard only once.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:12985-13018", "next_segment_id": "lseg-13c34bdb164c", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-bce0b5377542", "segment_id": "lseg-1b4c3b2110d4", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Each section is heard only once."}}

segment.text: At the end of the test, candidates are given 10 minutes to transfer their answers to an answer sheet (if they take their test paper-based) or 2 minutes (at the end of the test of course) to re-check the answers (if they do so computer-delivered).

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:13018-13265", "next_segment_id": "lseg-be8b59e98f0f", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-1b4c3b2110d4", "segment_id": "lseg-13c34bdb164c", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "At the end of the test, candidates are given 10 minutes to transfer their answers to an answer sheet (if they take their test paper-based) or 2 minutes (at the end of the test of course) to re-check the answers (if they do so computer-delivered)."}}

segment.text: [ 23 ] [ 20 ] Test takers will lose marks for incorrect spelling and grammar.

segment.text: [ 24 ] Reading [ edit ] The Reading paper has three sections and texts totalling approximately 2,150–3,250 words.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:13343-13457", "next_segment_id": "lseg-c289f9800bce", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-be8b59e98f0f", "segment_id": "lseg-2759c2aca050", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 24 ] Reading [ edit ] The Reading paper has three sections and texts totalling approximately 2,150–3,250 words."}}

segment.text: There will be a variety of question types, such as multiple-choice, short-answer questions, identifying information, identifying writer's views, labelling diagrams, completing a summary using words taken from the text and matching information/headings/features in the text/sentence endings.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:13457-13748", "next_segment_id": "lseg-eb8f3539a7c9", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-2759c2aca050", "segment_id": "lseg-c289f9800bce", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "There will be a variety of question types, such as multiple-choice, short-answer questions, identifying information, identifying writer's views, labelling diagrams, completing a summary using words taken from the text and matching information/headings/features in the text/sentence endings."}}

segment.text: Test takers should be careful when writing down their answers as they will lose marks for incorrect spelling and grammar.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:13748-13870", "next_segment_id": "lseg-ec5b47174a63", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c289f9800bce", "segment_id": "lseg-eb8f3539a7c9", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "Test takers should be careful when writing down their answers as they will lose marks for incorrect spelling and grammar."}}

segment.text: Texts in IELTS Academic Three reading texts, which come from books, journals, magazines, newspapers and online resources written for non-specialist audiences.

segment.text: [ 25 ] Texts in IELTS General Training Section 1 contains two or three short texts or several shorter texts, which deal with everyday topics.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:14262-14384", "next_segment_id": "lseg-59930daa3567", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-c9a23e09a0d0", "segment_id": "lseg-2658c62f5d9b", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "For example, timetables or notices – things a person would need to understand when living in an English-speaking country."}}

segment.text: [ 54 ] Criticism [ edit ] One criticism revolves around the accessibility and affordability of the IELTS test.

segment.text: The cost of taking the test, which varies by region but is generally considered expensive, can be a major barrier for test-takers from developing countries.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:27874-28031", "next_segment_id": "lseg-8d7d5ce5ffe3", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-da75cbae6812", "segment_id": "lseg-cae64c6f47cb", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "The cost of taking the test, which varies by region but is generally considered expensive, can be a major barrier for test-takers from developing countries."}}

segment.text: [ 55 ] For many, the test is prohibitively expensive, particularly if they need to retake it multiple times to achieve their desired score.

idempotency_key: language.segment.created:{"segment": {"confidence": 1.0, "end_time": null, "locator": "chars:28031-28171", "next_segment_id": "lseg-52fe537379ff", "page_locator": "", "previous_segment_id": "lseg-cae64c6f47cb", "segment_id": "lseg-8d7d5ce5ffe3", "source_id": "lsource-7eeb720cdfd7", "start_time": null, "text": "[ 55 ] For many, the test is prohibitively expensive, particularly if they need to retake it multiple times to achieve their desired score."}}

segment.text: [ 56 ] In addition to cost, accessibility issues arise from the limited availability of IELTS test centers.
